---
title: "Teaching"
---

My teaching focuses on **AI for decision-making**: how data, models and AI systems can support decisions, and how AI itself changes the way **managers and consumers decide**. I teach at Grenoble INP – Génie Industriel, mostly at master's level, as well as in doctoral and professional training. Today about two thirds of my teaching is in English, for international students.

My courses combine two facets, mirroring my research: **economics**, to analyse the role of AI in organisations, markets and consumer choices; and **data science**, to build and evaluate the models that inform decisions. As generative tools make some technical skills easier to acquire, I put the emphasis on problem structuring, system architecture, understanding business needs and critical thinking.

## Economics

The economics courses give engineering students the tools to understand the environment of the firm: markets and competition, industrial organisation, vertical relations and platforms, market failures and sustainability. They increasingly address the economics of organisations and products that integrate AI: digital goods and ecosystems, the transformation of industrial organisations, and the trade-offs managers face when adopting new technologies. I use experimental economics in class — for instance choice experiments — to illustrate concepts, then formalise and analyse the data the students produced, and flipped-classroom sessions built on readings and case studies prepared by the students.

**Associated courses**

- ***Basic Economics for Sustainable Industrial Engineering*** — M1 international, Génie Industriel (in English). Markets and competition, consumer and producer, market failures, externalities and sustainable development.
- ***Industrial Economics for Industrial Engineering*** — M1 international, Génie Industriel (in English). Market structures, vertical relations, principal–agent, networks and platforms, introduction to econometrics.

## Data science

The data science courses cover the whole data chain — collection, storage, processing, description, analysis, prediction, prescription and visualisation — with a grounding in statistics and decision theory, a hypothetico-deductive approach and a strong requirement for reproducibility. The aim is to develop decision-support tools driven by the needs of the decision-maker, and to discuss critically when a model is fit for the decision it serves. All courses are taught in R.

**Associated courses**

- ***Advanced Discrete Choice Modelling*** — Doctoral School of Economics, Université Grenoble Alpes. Random utility models, multinomial logit and its extensions (mixed logit, latent class, GEV, hybrid choice models), choice experiments, willingness to pay, marginal effects and elasticities.
- ***Smart Analytics for Big Data*** — M2, Génie Industriel (in English). Big data management, data science project management, supervised and unsupervised learning, spatial and temporal data. Co-built with colleagues from LIG, G-SCOP and Polytechnique Montréal.
- **Machine Learning** — M1, Génie Industriel. Stakes of machine learning, overview of supervised methods, model evaluation, strengths and limits.
- **Data Engineering** — M1, Génie Industriel. Data science project management, technical management of data and results, visualisation, societal issues.
- **Statistics** — L3, Génie Industriel. Probability, descriptive and inferential statistics.
- ***Introduction to AI System Project Management*** — MIAI Summer School (international students). An interactive game on the life cycle of an AI project, and a data challenge on predicting injection-mould production costs.

## Professional training in AI

I am responsible for two AI programmes at Grenoble INP's professional training department, for engineers and managers who are to become the AI leads of their organisation.

::: {.cases}
::: {.case}
#### "AI and Applications" certificate
[18 days · RNCP certification · eligible for the French CPF]{.sector}

A complete programme to become an AI lead: methods, tools, project management and industrial case studies (health, energy, transport, industry). It covers both the technical and the organisational sides of AI projects — system architecture, project management, skills, environmental, social and regulatory issues. Linked to the MIAI label of the same name.
:::

::: {.case}
#### "AI for Industry"
[2 days · Grenoble INP continuing education]{.sector}

A short course on industrial use cases of AI: quality, maintenance, cost estimation, planning. Built on real cases from my work with manufacturing SMEs.
:::
:::

Both programmes use active learning, including serious games designed for the purpose. I also run 3-hour workshops for company leaders and engineers. See [AI for Industry](industry.qmd) for more on training and support to companies.

## Teaching innovation

Since 2021 I have developed active-learning formats: case studies, data challenges, flipped classrooms and **serious games** on the design of data and AI systems and their economic, organisational and sustainability implications. Course material is delivered on Moodle and [Caseine](https://moodle.caseine.org/), with interactive simulations in R Shiny and personalised automatic quizzes built with R/exams; these resources are shared with the Caseine community.

International collaborations have shaped several courses: *Smart Analytics for Big Data* with Polytechnique Montréal, two online courses including a MOOC on industrial applications of AI for EIT Manufacturing, and courses created with Politecnico di Torino.
